# NLP pipeline on real résumé PDFs (generated by `python -m app.eval.kaggle_resume`; do not edit by hand)

Kaggle Resume Dataset: 2484 PDFs in 24 job categories, English, no JD and no relevance label (licence not stated: data kept in .runtime, aggregates only). The pipeline is the one the app runs on an upload: read_file (pypdf) → normalize → redact → sections/dates → chunks → skills.

## Reading and structure

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| PDFs read without error | 2484/2484 (100.0%) |
| Text vs the dataset's own text of the same résumé (token F1, median) | 1.000 |
| ... CVs with token F1 ≥ 0.9 | 99.8% |
| An experience section found | 99.0% |
| Dated roles parsed (years computed) | 97.7% |
| At least one known skill | 9.3% |
| CVs with personal data redacted | 58.9% |
| Median words after processing | 758 |

Quality flags raised: few_skills 2444, no_dated_roles 57, no_experience_section 24, short_text 1, garbled_text 1, prompt_injection 1

## False positives: testing tools in other trades

Categories where automation tools can legitimately appear: ENGINEERING, INFORMATION-TECHNOLOGY. In the other 2246 CVs, a detected test-automation tool is most likely a false positive, and passing the knock-out of an Automation Test JD is the failure that would matter to HR.

| Group | CVs | ≥ 1 testing tool detected | passes `selenium + java` | passes `playwright / cypress` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IT + engineering | 238 | 5.0% | 1.3% | 0.0% |
| all other trades | 2246 | 1.6% | 0.0% | 0.0% |

Tools detected in the other trades (what to check for gazetteer false positives): requests ×27, jmeter ×2, selenium ×2, uft ×2, cucumber ×2, espresso ×1, gatling ×1, junit ×1, postman ×1
